full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1-6 and respondent No. 7 instituted Title Suit No. 85 of 2002 for partition on declaration of title claiming a saham for 1.45 acres of land described in the schedule to the plaint. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Kader Sarder and Kasiruddin Sarder alias Basir Sarder. The owners died just before the R.S. operation. Abdul Kader Sarder got 1.88 acres of land in his eight annas share. After that, he died leaving behind a son, Alef Sarder and a daughter Saju Bibi. Alef Sarder surreptitiously got the entire land recorded in his name in the R.S. khatian excluding the name of his sister Saju Kasiruddin Sarder alias Basiruddin Sarder died leaving behind two sons; Samiruddin Sarder and Abdul Flamed Sarder and two daughters, Sonaban Bibi and Maju Bibi and widow Baru Bibi. Each son got .55 acre of land, each daughter got 27½ acre of land and widow got 23 acre of land. The R.S. khatian was correctly prepared in the names of the heirs of Kasiruddin Alef Sarder died leaving behind wife Rabeya, sister, Saju Bibi and paternal uncle's sons, Samiruddin and Hamed Saju Bibi transferred her share to her son, plaintiff No. 1 by a registered deed of gift dated 19.12.1952. Samiruddin transferred 06 acre of land to the plaintiffs and Saju Bibi out of his share. In this way, the plaintiff's became owner of 1.60, acres of land which they have been possessing in ejmali. Out of the suit land .36 acre of land was acquired for road belonging to C and B and accordingly, after proportionate deduction, the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing 1.45 acres of land. The S.A. khatian was not correctly prepared even then the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in their shares have not been affected. The plaintiffs did not have knowledge about wrong recording of the khatian and that for peaceful possession of the suit land, they demanded partition but the defendants refused to do so. Hence, the suit has been filed. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Alef Sarder had 8 annas share and accordingly, the R. S. khatian and S. A. khatian have been correctly prepared. Named Sarder Samiruddin and the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff's, Alef Sarder, sold .54 and .35 acres of land out of R. S. khatian Nos. 311 and 315 by registered deeds of sale dated 07.06.1946 and 17.07.1943 to Umesh Chandra Saha and the said land was again purchased by Abdul limed Sarder alone by two registered deeds dated 03.07.1954 and 04.07.1955. Accordingly, Abdul Hamed Sarder acquired 1.17½ acres of land and Aid Sarder had the remain Nos.  1.52½ acres of land. Alef Sarder died leaving behind widow Rabeya Bibi, Sister Saju Bibi and the cousins, the defendants Rabeya Bibi being the owner of 38½ acre of land sold .43 acre of land to Abdul Named Sarder Saju Bibi being the owner of .76 acre of land sold .12 acre of land to Hamed Sarder on 09.12.1952. Maju Bibi sold .28 acre of land to Samiruddin, who was the son of Kasiruddin Sarder. Samiruddin Sarder sold .30 acre of land to Bimol Chandra Roy, who again transferred the said land to Hamed Sarder Hamed Sarder acquired 2.84 acres of land by inheritance and purchase, who died leaving behind one son, two daughters and widow Sonaban Bibi as his heirs. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land. Therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
